title: Interacting Tomonaga-Lüttinger liquid with impurity for interaction constant $K = 1/2$: Thermopower investigation, entropy variation and heat capacity densities associated with thermoelectric particle transport
authors: Abdellah Touati, Redoune Zamoum, Farhi Houssam Eddine
abstract: We investigate thermoelectric and thermodynamic properties of a Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid with interaction parameter $K=1/2$ in the presence of a localized impurity. Using bosonization and refermionization, we derive an exact expression for the thermopower in the nonlinear regime and obtain the corresponding Seebeck coefficient in linear response. At low temperature, the Seebeck coefficient follows a Mott-like relation governed by the energy dependence of the transmission coefficient and is found to be closely related to the entropy per particle. This connection allows us to derive using Kelvin formula the thermopower contribution to the entropy density variation and the charge-carriers contribution to the heat capacity density. Both quantities exhibit Mott-like behavior in the low-temperature regime. We apply our results to a fractional quantum Hall quantum point contact and to a one-channel quantum conductor coupled to an Ohmic environment. Our results demonstrate the close connection between thermoelectric transport and thermodynamic properties in interacting one-dimensional quantum systems.
summary: This theoretical work analyzes the thermoelectric and thermodynamic properties of an interacting Tomonaga-Lüttinger liquid with an impurity. Using advanced field-theoretic methods, the authors derive relationships showing that the thermopower, entropy variation, and heat capacity all exhibit characteristic Mott-like behavior at low temperatures. The findings unify concepts of quantum transport and mesoscopic thermodynamics in 1D correlated systems.
main_problem: The paper investigates the thermoelectric and thermodynamic properties associated with particle transport in an interacting Tomonaga-Lüttinger liquid (TLL) containing an impurity.
main_result: The study establishes a close link between thermoelectric transport (thermopower) and thermodynamic quantities (entropy variation and heat capacity), showing both exhibit Mott-like behavior at low temperatures.
method: The analysis employs bosonization and refermionization techniques to derive exact expressions for transport coefficients in both linear and nonlinear regimes.
model_or_system: The primary model is an interacting TLL with an impurity, specifically analyzed for the interaction constant K=1/2. Applications include a quantum point contact between an FQH edge state and a normal metal, and a one-channel conductor coupled to an Ohmic environment.
key_observables: Thermopower (Q), Seebeck coefficient, Entropy variation (ΔS), and Heat capacity density (C).
important_parameters: Interaction constant K=1/2, low-temperature limit, and the energy dependence of the transmission coefficient.
main_assumptions: The analysis utilizes the Sommerfeld approximation for low temperatures and relies on mapping the system to a solvable TLL model.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the temperature and bias voltage dependence of the thermopower, and show the variation of the heat capacity density (C) versus temperature and Fermi energy for both QPC and OCC systems.
paper_structure: The paper systematically covers the theoretical framework, derives transport coefficients using Landauer formalism, analyzes the temperature and bias dependence of Q, ΔS, and C, and concludes by applying the results to specific quantum point contact and conductor models.
why_interesting: The explicit connection derived between non-equilibrium transport (thermopower) and equilibrium thermodynamics (heat capacity/entropy) in a strongly correlated 1D system provides a powerful tool for understanding energy dissipation in quantum conductors.
